newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Emsan group targets 40-pct rise in 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: Turk Emsan group targets 40-pct rise in 1997 sales.

text.p: Turkey's leading stainless steel kitchenware producer Emsan group is targeting an increase in its total sales of 40 percent on German mark basis in 1997, a senior company official said.

"We are planning to increase domestic turnover by 28 percent and export turnover by 60 percent, on DM bases. Rise in total sales will be 40 percent again on DM basis," Rupert Paller, chief executive officer of the company, told Reuters.
The total turnover of the group, which comprises Emsan Besyildiz Celik and Emsan Paslanmaz Celik, was 60 million marks in 1996, including 20 million marks of exports.
"Orders received for the first three months showed us that our sales structure will change this year and exports will have a bigger share than 33 percent in 1996," Paller said.
Emsan group is the domestic market leader in kitchenware with an approximate 25 percent share. The group owns three other companies, two in local marketing and one in foreign trade.

Partial shares of both companies are listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange. Emsan Besyildiz shares closed at 3,550 lira and Emsan Paslanmaz at 3,300 lira on Tuesday, compared to 3,550 and 3,250 lira on Monday.
Emsan group was taken over by Nardale Investment Ltd of Ireland in mid-1995 following financial bottlenecks.
Paller said the average capacity utilisation in 1996 was 71 percent. "But it was boosted in the last quarter, which means that our capacity utilisation is in a rapidly increasing trend," he added.
The capacity utilisation of both companies sank to around 30 percent in 1995 because of financial troubles.
"The main reason behind the low capacity utilisation in 1995 was the closure of one of the main plants. We reopened it after mid-1996. This made the capacity utilisation climb," Paller said.
He said investment was also made to modernise the production lines. A separate investment made for teflon-coating in one of the production lines became operational two weeks ago.
"Our initial machinery investments were aimed at increasing capacity utilisation because different production phases had varying capacities," he said.

"When this year's investments are completed, we will equalise the speeds of the different production phases. This operation will push up the capacity utilisation and expand the overall capacity at the same time," he added.
The new management increased the work force to 1,700 in 1996 from previous 900 by reopening a closed plant and adding new shifts.
The group signed an agreement in 1995 with a group of creditor banks to reschedule its overdue debts on a monthly payment basis for four years.
"Our total debts lessened throughout 1996 while we were investing three million DM and we will continue to invest in 1997 besides debt repayments," Paller said.
